Failures independently checked for exact leaked identity, limit restoration, controls, bounds and cleanup.

interpretation: Native ARM64 16 KiB execution is now observed for these specific experimental application probes. It does not establish full experimental Binder or general runtime compatibility.

The native lowered-limit control passes because the kernel close_range CLOEXEC operation succeeds. Forced TRAP returns ENOSYS and exposes the already recorded fallback scan-bound defect in both spawn APIs; both rounds restore the original soft/hard limits and preserve the parent FD.
This is the same boundary found on 4 KiB environments, not evidence that 16 KiB pages caused the leak. No runtime fix, clean Bun build, Release or distributionReady transition occurred.
All six forced termination cases reap the immediate child and remove its workspace. The test-only package was uninstalled with zero remaining processes under its UID.
